newsitem.title: NORWAY: Activists blockade Norske Skog plant.
newsitem.headline: Activists blockade Norske Skog plant.

text.p: A group of environmentalists from groups around Europe stopped traffic into one of Norske Skogindustrier's largest factories on Monday, saying the forestry group was a threat to Norway's biodiversity.
Around 30 activists sat in entrances and used chains to block truck deliveries into the company's plant at Follum in Hoenefoss, north of the Norwegian capital Oslo.
Jo Filseth, Norske Skog's director at the factory, told the NTB news agency that the action could cause disruption to production.
"If the activists are planning to stay here a long time, we have to consider what we are going to do. We hope it won't be necessary to involve the police," NTB quoted Filseth as saying.

The environmentalists -- from Norway's Nature and Youth, Britain's Reforest the Earth and Forest Action Network, Germany's Robin Wood and Pro Regenwald and the Finnish Nature League and Greenpeace Finland -- charge that most Norwegian forests have been turned into mono-cultural tree farms with nearly 900 species on the Norwegian Red List of threatened species.
They said Norske Skog, as Europe's third largest paper manufacturer, should buy only old-growth free wood, which, they claimed, is sourced from forests areas managed in an ecologically sound manner.

"The Norske Skog company is a threat to Norway's biodiversity," a statement from Nature and Youth said. "The majority of the annual timber harvest in Norway is processed by Norske Skog's factories. In addition Norske Skog buys from other countries. Because of its size, Norske Skog has a tremendous responsibility to live up to Norway's international commitments."
Silje Schei Tveitdal, head of Nature and Youth in Oslo, told Reuters that the protestors planned to remain at the plant for the remainder of the day.
